# Proka Executable

## Lead-in {.unnumbered .unlisted}
This part generally describes:

- the PKE's basic structure;
- the elements of PKE;
- the sequence of each element in PKE format;
- the ways to parse/construct an valid PKE format;

Some tips of reading this part:

1. Notice the structure of each element, which may be frequently used in your development;
2. The ways to help you parse/construct PKE is very useful for you to write your own parser/builder.

---

This part is intended for:

- **Linker developers** who want to support PKE as an output file;
- **Operating system developers** who want to add support for running PKE binaries;
- **Compiler backend developers** (to emit PKE object / executable);
- **Reverse engineers** who need to inspect and analyze PKE binaries;
- **Toolchain maintainers** working on ProkaOS tooling;
- **Application developers** who want to understand how PKE executables work under the hood;
